units.function: Embedded-Postgres end-to-end tests for automatically provisioning the default Local execution environment, leasing it to a Heartbeat Run, releasing the lease, and injecting Paperclip control-plane identity variables into a process adapter.
units.dependencyDirection: heartbeatService selects/creates an Environment, records an EnvironmentLease, launches the process adapter on the server host, injects run-scoped environment variables and a generated API credential, then updates Run context and releases the lease.
units.keyDataModels: Instance-scoped Local Environment, Run-bound EnvironmentLease status/provider/releasedAt, Run context environment projection, process command/arguments, Agent/Company/Run identifiers, API URL and PAPERCLIP_API_KEY generated from a server JWT secret.
units.lifecycle: An on-demand process Run creates or reuses one default Local environment, acquires a lease, executes an arbitrary configured host process, records environment/lease identifiers in context, releases the lease at terminal success, and exposes Agent, Company, Run, API URL and an API key in the child process environment.
units.testAssessment: Two end-to-end cases prove happy-path Local environment creation, lease release and expected process environment injection. Missing are concurrent/exclusive lease behavior, crash/kill/timeout/cancellation, orphan detection and expiry, server restart, failed acquisition/release, host filesystem/network/process isolation, command authorization, environment inheritance and secret leakage, token claims/audience/scope/TTL/revocation/rotation, per-Work permission and data contracts, remote execution attestation, cleanup of the created temp directory, and non-local drivers. Credential presence is asserted, but its least privilege is not.
units.designRationale: Give every Run an explicit execution-environment lifecycle even for simple local development, expose enough identity for the Agent to call back into the control plane, and retain a lease record for cleanup and observability.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs interchangeable local/customer/cloud execution nodes with fenced leases, short-lived runtime identity and auditable capability/data boundaries, without assuming the control plane may execute arbitrary commands on its own host.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit EnvironmentPort, acquire/renew/release lease lifecycle and Run-bound environment attestation. Treat host-local process execution as an opt-in development adapter, never the production default. Issue a one-time, short-TTL, audience-bound RuntimeCapability token containing exact Work/attempt/Connector/tool/data scopes and proof key; keep the signing secret outside child environments, support revocation and renewal, redact all process output, and require sandbox/network/filesystem policy plus crash-safe lease fencing. Self-hosted execution nodes should attest independently to a cloud control plane.
units.responsibilityConflict: The fixture has responsibleUserId but no human authorization or responsibility contract controls the host command or credential issuance. A generic API key is injected into an arbitrary process and the test does not prove least privilege, while a successful process exit is treated as sufficient lifecycle success without result/evidence validation. Local lease state provides observability, not runtime isolation or legal/business accountability.
